chapter: Eddie South, high school and the South Side scene
title: Generations of Chicago trumpeters and drummers around Louis Armstrong
summary: Taylor and Hinton place Oliver, Keppard, Louis, Guy Kelly, and the drummers Zutty, Baby Dodds, Tubby Hall and others in order.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Explain something to me about generations. The Louis Armstrong… well King Oliver and Freddy Kephard, now they were around the same age?
Yes.
Okay, so they were older then Louis?
Yes. They were older then Louis.
They were older then Louis. Who else would be in their generation, like that … Sidney Mashay, would he be in that… or was he younger?
He was young but he didn‟t get to Chicago. He went another way.
I see.
I‟ll tell you who, Boone Johnson.
Boone Johnson, okay.
He was in that age bracket. Then there was Louis, then there was Guy Kelly, this was my friend. Fabulous young friend from Baton Rouge. He was very much on the way as much as Louis but he didn‟t…
Really, but he didn‟t quite make it.
He didn‟t… when Louis was still not known… he was out of Baton Rouge and I got to know him. He came to Chicago and did great with Gene …
Now was Zuly in that…
Zuly, yes. Zuly was a senior citizen. He was… he‟s in Louis era. That‟s the Hot Five. He was Louie‟s drummer. But Louie to the day he died… TAYLOR; Now who was before Zuly? Was it Baby Daz maybe?
Baby Daz was… and a guy named Curry.
Oh, yeah, right.
Baby Daz, Curry and Tubby Hall.
Tubby Hall, you‟re right, sure, sure.

Tubby Hall, yeah. Now there was another guy, he was terrible, he wasn‟t a good drummer. He was a policeman. When he played drums he just kind of bulldozed his way in there and lift the body because he was a cop, but he wasn‟t…
Wasn‟t good, yeah.
Then there was Floyd Campbell that came out.
